rows.subtopic: Common Salt and Chemicals from It
rows.stem: The chlorine produced during the electrolysis of brine solution is used in the manufacture of :
rows.solution:
Electrolysis of brine (the chlor-alkali process) gives sodium hydroxide, chlorine and hydrogen. Chlorine is used for water treatment, for disinfecting swimming pools, and in making PVC, pesticides, CFCs and disinfectants. Ammonia is not made from chlorine, Plaster of Paris comes from gypsum, and it is the sodium hydroxide, not the chlorine, that goes into soaps and detergents.

This is option (B) Disinfectants.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.subtopic: Defects of Vision and their Correction
rows.stem: A boy while reading a book, keeps it much beyond 25 cm from his eyes. This defect of vision has arised because of

options.label: A
options.text: excessive curvature of the eye lens

options.label: B
options.text: the focal length of the eye lens has increased

options.label: D
options.text: the focal length of the eye lens has become too small

rows.solution:
A boy who has to hold the book well beyond 25 cm cannot see nearby objects clearly, so he has hypermetropia (far-sightedness). It arises when the focal length of the eye lens is too long, or the eyeball has become too small, so the image of a near object forms behind the retina.

Excessive curvature of the lens, an elongated eyeball and a focal length that is too small all cause myopia instead.

This is option (B) the focal length of the eye lens has increased.

rows.stem:
A gas ‘X’ is found in the upper layer of atmosphere. It is a deadly poison, but still essential for all life forms on earth.

(a) Identify the gas and state the main factor for its depletion in the atmosphere.

(b) How is this gas formed in the upper atmosphere ?
rows.solution:
(a) X is ozone, \(\mathrm{O_3}\). At ground level it is a deadly poison, but in the upper atmosphere it shields the earth from the harmful ultraviolet radiation of the sun. The main factor for its depletion is the excessive use of synthetic chemicals such as chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs), used as refrigerants and in fire extinguishers.

(b) The higher energy ultraviolet radiation splits molecular oxygen into free oxygen atoms, which then combine with molecular oxygen to form ozone:

\(\mathrm{O_2 \xrightarrow{\text{UV}} O + O}\)

\(\mathrm{O + O_2 \rightarrow O_3}\)

rows.stem: Use Ohm’s law to determine the potential difference across the \(6\,\Omega\) resistor in the following circuit when key is closed :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the circuit is given only as a drawing: one loop holding a 6 V battery and a plug key, with resistors labelled 2 ohm and 6 ohm along the top wire and 4 ohm on the right-hand wire; how the resistors are connected is stated nowhere in the text. Page idx 14.
rows.solution:
In the circuit the 2 \(\Omega\), 6 \(\Omega\) and 4 \(\Omega\) resistors are in series with the 6 V battery, so the same current flows through all three.

Total resistance: \(R = R_1 + R_2 + R_3 = 2 + 6 + 4 = 12\,\Omega\).

By Ohm's law, \(I = \dfrac{V}{R} = \dfrac{6}{12} = 0{\cdot}5\) A.

Potential difference across the 6 \(\Omega\) resistor: \(V = IR = 0{\cdot}5 \times 6 = 3\) V.

rows.stem: Prove that if the current through a resistor is increased by 100%, then the increase in power dissipated through the resistor will be 300%.
rows.solution:
Power dissipated in a resistor is \(P_1 = I^2R\).

Increasing the current by 100% doubles it, to \(2I\). The new power is \(P_2 = (2I)^2R = 4I^2R\).

Increase in power: \(P_2 - P_1 = 4I^2R - I^2R = 3I^2R = 3P_1\).

Percentage increase: \(\dfrac{3P_1}{P_1} \times 100 = 300\%\).

rows.stem:
When an incident ray of light enters a medium ‘X’ from air, it bends towards the normal.

Infer about the following with respect to air :

(a) Optical density of medium ‘X’.

(b) Speed of light through medium ‘X’

Give reason for your answer in each case.
rows.solution:
(a) Medium X is optically denser than air. A ray going from a rarer medium into a denser medium bends towards the normal, and that is what the ray does on entering X.

(b) The speed of light in X is less than in air. Light travels more slowly in an optically denser medium (the refractive index of X, \(n = \dfrac{c}{v}\), is greater than 1), and slowing down is what makes the ray bend towards the normal.

rows.stem: Write chemical equation for the chemical reaction between the aqueous solutions of sodium sulphate and barium chloride. State two types of chemical reactions in which this reaction can be placed.
rows.solution:
\(\mathrm{Na_2SO_4(aq) + BaCl_2(aq) \rightarrow BaSO_4(s) + 2NaCl(aq)}\)

A white precipitate of barium sulphate forms. The reaction is:

(i) a double displacement reaction, since the two compounds exchange ions;

(ii) a precipitation reaction, since it produces an insoluble solid.

rows.stem: What is short circuiting ? State its possible causes. What is likely to happen if a domestic circuit gets short circuited ? Give reason for the justification of your answer.
rows.solution:
Short circuiting happens when the live wire and the neutral wire of a domestic circuit come into direct contact with each other.

Possible causes (any two): damaged insulation of the live and neutral wires; a fault in an electrical appliance; overloading of the circuit.

When a circuit is short circuited, its resistance falls to almost zero, so the current increases abruptly. The heat produced (\(H = I^2Rt\)) makes the fuse wire melt and break the circuit. Without a fuse, the wires would overheat and could cause a fire.

rows.stem: Differentiate between a gamete and a zygote. State their significance in sexual reproduction.
rows.solution:
| Gamete | Zygote |
|---|---|
| A germ cell (sex cell): the male or female reproductive cell | Formed by the fusion of a male gamete and a female gamete |
| Has half the number of chromosomes (one set) and half the DNA of a body cell, haploid (n) | Has two sets of chromosomes, diploid (2n) |

Significance: gametes carry half the chromosomes, so when two of them fuse the original number of chromosomes and the amount of DNA are restored in the next generation. The zygote grows and develops into a new organism with the same amount of DNA as its parents, and because it combines DNA from two parents it also carries variation.

rows.stem:
Give reasons for the following :

(a) Rate of breathing in aquatic animals is much faster than terrestrial organisms.

(b) Rings of cartilage are present in throat of human being.

(c) During anaerobic respiration, a 3 carbon molecule (compound) is formed as an end product instead of \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) in some cells of human beings.
rows.solution:
(a) The amount of oxygen dissolved in water is fairly low compared to the amount of oxygen in air, so aquatic animals have to breathe much faster to obtain enough oxygen.

(b) The rings of cartilage in the throat (the trachea or windpipe) ensure that the air passage does not collapse when there is little air in it.

(c) During vigorous activity our muscle cells run short of oxygen. The pyruvate (a three-carbon compound) formed from glucose is then converted into lactic acid, also a three-carbon compound, instead of being broken down to carbon dioxide and water:

Glucose \(\xrightarrow{\text{in cytoplasm}}\) pyruvate \(\xrightarrow{\text{lack of oxygen}}\) lactic acid + energy

rows.stem:
(a) Define the term “homologous series of carbon compounds”. Write a homologous series of compounds having functional group \(-\mathrm{CHO}\).

(b) Design an experiment to distinguish between an alcohol and a carboxylic acid. Also write chemical equation for that case in which reaction occurs.
rows.solution:
(a) A homologous series is a series of carbon compounds in which the same functional group substitutes for hydrogen in a carbon chain. Its members have the same general formula and similar chemical properties, and successive members differ by a \(\mathrm{CH_2}\) unit.

A homologous series with the \(-\mathrm{CHO}\) (aldehyde) group: methanal, \(\mathrm{HCHO}\); ethanal, \(\mathrm{CH_3CHO}\); propanal, \(\mathrm{C_2H_5CHO}\).

(b) Take the two samples in separate test tubes and add a spatula full of sodium hydrogencarbonate (or sodium carbonate) to each, then shake.

In the test tube with the carboxylic acid there is brisk effervescence of a colourless gas, carbon dioxide, which turns lime water milky. In the test tube with the alcohol nothing happens. Taking ethanoic acid as the acid:

\(\mathrm{CH_3COOH + NaHCO_3 \rightarrow CH_3COONa + CO_2 + H_2O}\)

rows.stem:
(a) Define the term “structural isomers”. Write the structures of two isomers of butane \((\mathrm{C_4H_{10}})\).

(b) Two carbon compounds X and Y have the molecular formula \(\mathrm{C_2H_4}\) and \(\mathrm{C_3H_8}\) respectively. Which one of the two is most likely to show addition reaction ? Justify your answer. Also give (i) chemical equation to explain the process of addition reaction in this case and (ii) name of the industry where this reaction is applied.
rows.solution:
(a) Structural isomers are carbon compounds with the same molecular formula but different structures.

Butane, \(\mathrm{C_4H_{10}}\), has two isomers:

1. n-butane, a straight chain: \(\mathrm{CH_3{-}CH_2{-}CH_2{-}CH_3}\). Four carbons in a row; the two end carbons carry three hydrogens each and the two middle carbons two each.

2. Isobutane (2-methylpropane), a branched chain: \(\mathrm{CH_3{-}CH(CH_3){-}CH_3}\). A chain of three carbons with the fourth carbon attached to the middle one; the middle carbon carries one hydrogen and each of the other three carbons carries three.

(b) X, \(\mathrm{C_2H_4}\) (ethene), is the one that shows addition reaction. It fits the formula \(\mathrm{C_nH_{2n}}\), so it is an unsaturated hydrocarbon with a carbon-carbon double bond, and atoms can add across that double bond. Y, \(\mathrm{C_3H_8}\) (propane), fits \(\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+2}}\): it is saturated, with only single bonds, so it does not undergo addition.

(i) Ethene adds hydrogen in the presence of a nickel or palladium catalyst:

\(\mathrm{CH_2{=}CH_2 + H_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Ni or Pd catalyst}} CH_3{-}CH_3}\)

(ii) This hydrogenation is used in the vegetable ghee industry, to convert vegetable oils into vegetable ghee.
